Care in the language families prefer

Centro Hispano de Salud is West Jefferson Medical Center’s Hispanic health program. It helps patients navigate appointments, preventive visits, and hospital services with bilingual support so language is not a barrier to care.

The Hispanic Health Center clinic at 3909 Lapalco Blvd. in Harvey (504-349-2150) is a neighborhood access point. For system-wide Hispanic health resources, see also Medical College of Wisconsin Hispanic Health Center.

To schedule, call the clinic or use Find a Provider. Hospital main number: 504-347-5511.

fields.value:
Otolaryngology on the Westbank

The Department of Otolaryngology — Head and Neck Surgery at West Jefferson Medical Center cares for ear, nose, and throat conditions across the lifespan. Patients come here for recurring infections, nasal blockage, voice and swallowing problems, sleep apnea, facial injury, and thyroid or parathyroid disease.

Whether the need is an acute illness, a chronic sinus condition, or evaluation of a neck mass, the ENT team works to diagnose the cause and match treatment to each patient’s goals — from medical management to in-office procedures and surgery when it is the better option.

How to make an appointment

Call the West Jefferson ENT clinic at 504-934-8550 to schedule, or find an otolaryngologist in the Medical College of Wisconsin provider directory.

West Jefferson Medical Center Ear, Nose & Throat
1111 Medical Center Blvd., Suite N-707
Marrero, LA 70072
Phone: 504-934-8550

Conditions we treat

Common reasons patients are referred to ENT at West Jefferson include:

  • Recurring ear infections, hearing loss, tinnitus, and balance concerns
  • Chronic sinusitis, nasal polyps, allergic rhinitis, and nasal obstruction
  • Tonsillitis, snoring, obstructive sleep apnea, and voice or swallowing difficulty
  • Thyroid nodules and tumors, parathyroid disease, and neck masses
  • Facial injury and selected cosmetic or reconstructive needs of the face and eyelids

Treatments and procedures

Care plans start with a focused exam and, when needed, in-office endoscopy or imaging. Medical therapy is used whenever it can control symptoms. When procedures are appropriate, the team offers a range of ear, nose, throat, and neck operations, including:

Ear

Evaluation and treatment for infection, hearing, and related ear conditions, coordinated with audiology when testing is part of the workup.

Nose

Medical and surgical options for sinus disease, polyps, and nasal obstruction, aimed at restoring breathing and reducing repeat infections.

Throat

Care for tonsil and adenoid disease, snoring and sleep apnea, and voice or swallowing disorders, including procedures when conservative care is not enough.

Neck and face

  • Thyroidectomy and parathyroidectomy
  • Neck dissection and thyroglossal duct excision
  • Hyoid suspension for selected sleep-related airway problems
  • Blepharoplasty and therapeutic Botox when clinically indicated

What to expect

Bring a list of medications, prior imaging or sleep studies, and questions about recovery time. If surgery is recommended, your surgeon will review benefits, risks, and after-care before you decide. For hospital campus parking and visitor hours, see Patients & Visitors.

A regular doctor close to home

West Jefferson Medical Center primary care physicians help patients prevent illness, manage chronic conditions, and coordinate specialty care. Clinics offer same- and next-day appointments, in-clinic and virtual visits, and on-site lab and imaging when you need testing in one trip.

Clinic phones

  • Internal medicine on campus (Suite S-850): 504-349-6450
  • Lapalco / Harvey: 504-349-6900
  • Oakwood / Terrytown: 504-349-6925
  • Algiers: 504-368-4066
  • Manhattan / Harvey: 504-349-6930

After 5 p.m. or on weekends, consider Medical College of Wisconsin Urgent Care. Find a primary care provider.

fields.name: Detail
fields.value:
Fast stroke response

West Jefferson Medical Center is designated a Comprehensive Stroke Center by The Joint Commission. Emergency teams, neuroscience specialists, and rehabilitation staff work together from first symptoms through recovery.

If you suspect a stroke, call 911. Do not drive yourself. For non-emergency questions about stroke services, call the hospital at 504-347-5511. Learn more about the Medical College of Wisconsin Neuroscience Institute.
